ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, AB is the diameter of the semicircle O, D is a point on the semicircle O, C is the midpoint of the arc $\overset{\frown}{BD}$, connecting AC intersects BD at point E, connecting AD, if $BE = 4DE$ and $CE = 6$, what is the length of AB?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, extend OC to intersect BD at K, and connect BC.\\
Since $\overset{\frown}{CD} = \overset{\frown}{BC}$,\\
it follows that OC$\perp$BD.\\
Given BE=4DE,\\
we can assume DE=k, BE=4k, then DK=BK=2.5k, EK=1.5k.\\
Since AB is the diameter,\\
it implies $\angle$ADK=$\angle$DKC=$\angle$ACB=$90^\circ$,\\
thus AD$\parallel$CK,\\
which leads to AE: EC=DE: EK,\\
therefore, AE: 6=k: 1.5k,\\
hence, AE=4.\\
Since $\triangle$ECK$\sim$$\triangle$EBC,\\
it follows that EC$^{2}$=EK$\cdot$EB,\\
thus, 36=1.5k$\cdot$4k.\\
Given k>0,\\
we find k=$\sqrt{6}$,\\
therefore, BC=$\sqrt{{BE}^{2}-{EC}^{2}}=\sqrt{96-36}=2\sqrt{15}$,\\
hence, AB=$\sqrt{{AC}^{2}+{BC}^{2}}=\sqrt{{10}^{2}+{(2\sqrt{15})}^{2}}=\boxed{4\sqrt{10}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is an upper semicircle, AB is the horizontal diameter, and O is marked on AB; D is on the left circular arc, and C is on the upper circular arc; segment AC and segment BD intersect at E, and AD has been connected. Reasoning: According to the problem, draw auxiliary line OC, intersecting BD at K, and connect BC. Because C is the midpoint of arc BD, arc CD = arc CB, and the line OC from the circle center O to chord BD perpendicularly bisects BD; therefore K is the midpoint of BD and OC ⟂ BD. Let DE = k, then BE = 4k, BD = 5k, so DK = BK = 2.5k. In the figure E is between D and K, therefore EK = DK - DE = 1.5k. Since AB is the diameter, ∠ADB = 90°, and K is on BD, so ∠ADK = 90°; meanwhile OC ⟂ BD, so ∠DKC = 90°, hence AD ∥ CK. From AD ∥ CK, and A, E, C are collinear, D, E, K are collinear, it can be obtained that △ADE ∼ △CKE, therefore AE:EC = DE:EK = k:1.5k = 2:3. It is known that EC = 6, so AE = 4, AC = AE + EC = 10. Also because AB is the diameter and C is on the semicircle, ∠ACB = 90°. In △ECK and △EBC, ∠EKC = ∠ECB = 90°, and ∠CEK = ∠CEB, so △ECK ∼ △EBC, thus EC² = EK·EB. Substituting EC = 6, EK = 1.5k, EB = 4k, obtain 36 = 1.5k·4k = 6k², so k = √6. Thus EB = 4√6. In right triangle EBC, BC = √(EB² - EC²) = √(96 - 36) = 2√15. Finally in right triangle ACB, AB = √(AC² + BC²) = √(10² + (2√15)²) = √160 = 4√10.
